subject: DPA and transfer terms — logs, embeddings, subprocessors, and execution flow
messages:

Cc: p.gomez@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA review — embeddings + telemetry questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA. A couple of items our legal/privacy team flagged that we need clarity on before we can proceed to execution:

1) Role designation for embeddings and derived vectors. We need to confirm whether Redwood will be acting as a processor for embeddings generated from Acme data, and whether derivative embeddings are considered controller data or processor outputs.

2) Logs and telemetry: please confirm retention windows for request/response logs and whether telemetry (latency, error rates, usage metrics) may contain any persistent identifiers tied to Acme. We need explicit retention ceilings and deletion guarantees.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: can you provide the current subprocessor list for the EU region and confirm whether transfers will rely on SCCs or another lawful basis? Also, how do you notify customers of new subprocessors and obtain approvals?

Attached is a short redline from our side focusing on those sections — see DPA-Acme-Redline-v1.pdf. We want to keep this moving; what timeline do you need to get to an executed DPA (DocuSign preferred)?

Best,
Lina

From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2026-10-13T08:30:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA review — embeddings + telemetry questions

Quick notes after reviewing Lina's redline and our template:

1) Role on embeddings: our standard position is that Redwood acts as a processor for customer-supplied inputs and any generated embeddings derived directly from those inputs. We can add explicit language: "Redwood will process Customer Content as Processor; embeddings generated from Customer Content are Processor Outputs and remain subject to Customer's control and deletion requests." Suggest adding a short definition block: "Processor Outputs: machine-generated embeddings, tokens, or derived artifacts created from Customer Content."

2) Logs & telemetry: propose the following retained language: request/response logs retained for up to 30 days by default; telemetry (metrics aggregated, latency/error rates) retained up to 12 months and stored in anonymized, aggregated form without persistent customer identifiers. For customers with stricter needs we can offer configurable retention via Dedicated/Private deployments or contract amendment. We should expose an SLA for deletion request response time (e.g., 30 days) and add a clause mandating scrubbing of any customer identifiers upon request.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: we maintain an up-to-date subprocessor list published at https://status.redwoodinference.com/subprocessors (include in DPA). For EU transfers we rely on the European Commission SCCs as the primary lawful basis; we will execute SCCs where required and provide signed SCCs upon request. We notify customers of new subprocessors 30 days in advance and allow a limited right to object.

4) Minor redlines: tighten definitions for Controller vs Processor to avoid ambiguity where customers run model training vs inference. Add explicit carveouts for telemetry used in aggregate product improvement (anonymized), with an option for customers to opt-out via specific contract terms.

Action items: Monica to prepare a cohesive redline PDF (v2) that incorporates these points; Monica, can you also confirm whether we can reduce default log retention to 14 days for enterprise customers if requested?

Laura Bennett
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

Laura / Irene,

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our side:

• Embeddings as Processor Outputs: agreed in principle, but we need clarity on derivative embeddings created by model prompting across multiple customer inputs (e.g., cross-customer vectorization). Can you confirm that embeddings created from a mix of customer inputs will be logically segregated and not accessible to other customers?

• Telemetry identifiers: good to hear about anonymization. Please can you confirm that IP addresses and request IDs are not stored long-term and that any sampling used for metrics will not retain raw request payloads.

• Subprocessor notice: 30 days is acceptable. Please share the current EU subprocessor list and the contact for escalations if we object to a new subprocessor.

Also — our procurement team prefers DocuSign for execution. Please send an envelope when ready and we'll route it internally.

Peter Gomez
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Health

Subject: Final DPA redline and DocuSign for execution

Hi Lina / Peter — thanks for the quick feedback and the clarifying questions. Per Laura's guidance we've incorporated the agreed language and added a short section addressing cross-customer separation for embeddings and sampling/retention rules for telemetry. Highlights:

• Controller/Processor definitions: added explicit "Processor Outputs" definition and a cross-customer segregation clause: "Redwood will not use embeddings generated from a Customer's inputs to service other customers in a way that would reveal Customer-specific data; embeddings used for global model improvements will be aggregated and cannot be reverse-engineered to recover Customer Content."

• Logs & telemetry: revised defaults to 30 days for request/response logs (can be reduced to 14 days by contract), telemetry metrics retained 12 months in anonymized/aggregated form; IPs/request IDs not retained past 7 days unless required for security investigations (with notice).

• Subprocessors & transfers: attached current EU subprocessor list (SCCs-reference.pdf) and link to published list. We will execute SCCs as the transfer mechanism and will issue 30-day notices for new subprocessors. Escalation contact: privacy-escalations@redwoodinference.com.

I've attached the consolidated redline (DPA-Acme-Redline-v3.pdf). If the wording looks good I will prepare a DocuSign envelope and share the link here.

Next steps: please confirm by EOD Monday and I'll send DocuSign.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
